item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is the preferable patch because it keeps upload behavior localized to FilesService and centralizes request handling in one private path. Neither candidate fully satisfies the frozen contract, but B additionally duplicates Add logic and makes a broad, explicitly out-of-scope retry-layer change.","reasons":["A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile and verifies the multipart field, filename, content, and replay after a 429 using an os.File source.","A keeps option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors shared through its add helper; B copies that machinery into Upload, creating two implementations that can drift.","B modifies RawClient retry and reader-ownership semantics for every seekable request body, contrary to the contract's instruction not to refactor unrelated retry machinery.","B's generic replay implementation reuses and seeks the same reader from GetBody instead of producing an independent body, expanding maintenance and behavioral risk beyond file uploads."],"risks_a":["Upload calls the new private add helper rather than routing through the existing public Add method as explicitly required.","Add now eagerly buffers every caller-encoded body, changing its streaming and memory behavior despite the requirement to preserve Add behavior.","The tests omit explicit Upload validation and source-reader failure cases, and the original Add method/path assertions were effectively moved rather than preserved for Add."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses Add and duplicates its option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error logic.","The RawClient change is broad scope expansion and changes closing semantics for seekable readers across the SDK.","The tests do not cover source-reader failures for Upload; the retry test uses an already replayable buffered multipart body, while separate raw-layer tests justify machinery the contract excludes."]}
